reasons.specificity: The inventory maps named conditionals to specific passages—Jaeggi's 'in so far as problems have been solved,' Roth's 'only if,' Kuhn's instrumental 'if by knowledge we mean knowing how'—and assigns speaker, scope, and modal force individually rather than summarising generic themes about progress.
reasons.anchoring: All fourteen findings include verbatim quotations that directly carry the conditional wording (if, only if, in so far as, when); the interpretations placed on them—sufficient condition, necessary condition, evaluative permission—are supported by the quoted language rather than imported from outside the text.
reasons.non_obviousness: The inventory usefully distinguishes modal force (evaluative permission vs. causal law), identifies that no relation reaches biconditional status, and traces how the know-how reply is qualified by the scientific-community dependency—distinctions a casual reader is unlikely to isolate without prompting.
reasons.coherence: Speaker attribution is consistent throughout both tables and the prose (Jaeggi's stated relations, Chen's critical inferences, Roth and Kuhn as attributed); modal labels ('can be regarded,' 'can simultaneously mean') match the quoted anchors and are not strengthened in the findings ledger.
reasons.usefulness: The two-table structure (conditional-relation inventory plus nesting/exceptions/counterexamples) directly serves a reader working through Chen's argument, correctly preserving the asymmetry between sufficient and necessary conditions and identifying the three philosophical counterexamples without collapsing them into causal claims.
reasons.hallucination_risk: No invented consensus, false contradiction, or unsupported relation is detectable; the analysis correctly notes the absence of biconditionals, does not attribute to Jaeggi claims made only by Chen, and the counterexample cases (marriage, childhood, Nazism) are all verbatim-anchored in the source.

score.one_line: A well-anchored, speaker-differentiated conditional inventory that correctly distinguishes modal force, avoids causal recast, and preserves the paper's asymmetric sufficient/necessary structure across both tables.
